title: Phrae With Kids: 3-Day Family Plan, Thailand | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 3-day, 2-night Phrae family itinerary for travelers with kids: old teak mansions, the Phae Mueang Phi badlands, Wat Phra That Cho Hae, plus farm cafes and a water park. Real opening hours and entry fees included.
keywords: Phrae with kids, Phrae family trip, Phae Mueang Phi, Wat Phra That Cho Hae, Phrae teak houses
h1:
Phrae With Kids
3 Days, 2 Nights the Whole Family Will Enjoy
intro: Phrae is a small, easy town to get around. The distances between sights are short, so there's no long time in the car and the kids don't get fussy. This plan pairs the things grown-ups love, like the old teak mansions and Wat Phra That Cho Hae, with spots where kids can actually run around: the Phae Mueang Phi badlands, a farm cafe, and a water park. We fit it all into 3 days and 2 nights without rushing.

blocks.html: What makes Phrae great for families is that everything sits close together. You can walk between the sights in the old town, while Phae Mueang Phi and Cho Hae are only 10–15 km from the center, just a few minutes by car. That's a big help for little ones who can't handle long drives. We've arranged the plan to alternate: cultural sights in the morning when it's still cool, then save the activities where kids burn off energy for the afternoon.

blocks.title: Before you set out
blocks.html: Many of the teak houses are old buildings with wooden floors and steep stairs. Bring shoes that slip off easily (some houses ask you to remove them before going up) and keep a hand on small children. At Phae Mueang Phi the midday sun is strong, so pack a hat and drinking water.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Old town, teak mansions, then a kid-friendly cafe

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Old town + teak mansions + kids' cafe

items.activity: Start at Khum Chao Luang (the Phrae city museum) in the heart of the old town
items.note: A pale-blue European-style building that's easy to walk through, with a wide courtyard where kids can wander and the photos come out great

items.activity: Walk on to Baan Vongburi, a pink teak mansion over 120 years old
items.note: Open 09:00–16:00, entry 30 THB for adults and 10 THB for kids. The house is full of objects, so tell the kids to look but not touch

items.activity: Lunch on khanom sen nam ngiao with khao kaep in the old-town quarter
items.note: Phrae's nam ngiao isn't very spicy, so kids can eat it. If you're worried about heat, ask for the chili on the side

items.activity: Head to Baan Pratabjai (the House of a Hundred Pillars), with over 130 huge teak posts under the floor
items.note: Open 08:00–17:00, entry 15 THB for Thais. Kids love walking among the giant pillars and there's plenty of room to run

items.activity: Finish at The Pool Sky, a cafe with a water-play area for kids
items.note: Water play is 99 THB per person with no time limit, and there's poolside seating so parents can sip a coffee and watch the kids up close

items.activity: Dinner in town, then back to the hotel to rest
items.note: Kids who've played in the water all afternoon usually fall asleep easily

blocks.html: Day one stays mostly in town. The walk between Khum Chao Luang, Baan Vongburi, and the restaurants is very short. If you have a stroller you can push it along the sidewalks, but some stretches are uneven, so it's easier to carry younger kids part of the way.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Phae Mueang Phi, Cho Hae, then a farm cafe

items.activity: Head out to Phae Mueang Phi early to beat the heat, about 15 km from town
items.note: Open 08:00–17:00, entry 20 THB for adults and 10 THB for kids. The oddly shaped earth pillars look like another planet, and kids find it exciting

items.activity: Walk the trail through the forest park, which doesn't take long
items.note: The path is sandy soil, so keep a hand on small children. Some viewpoints have high edges, so don't let kids run near them

items.activity: Drive back into town for lunch and a break from the heat
items.note: Try khao soi or a mild Phrae-style noodle soup the kids can eat too

items.activity: Go up to Wat Phra That Cho Hae, the temple of those born in the Year of the Tiger
items.note: Open 06:00–19:00. The golden stupa stands 33 m tall, and there's a lift for the elderly and wheelchair users (20 THB) — handy if you're bringing grandparents along

items.activity: On the way down, stop at The Phrae Farm, a farm cafe with gardens and photo spots
items.note: There's a vineyard, a cocoa garden, and open space for kids to run, a good place to stretch out before heading back

items.activity: Back into town for an easy dinner
items.note: If the kids still have energy, swing by the evening walking street (if it's on that day) to graze on snacks

blocks.text: Day 3 — Indigo dyeing, souvenirs, head home

items.activity: Go to Baan Thung Hong, the indigo (mo hom) cloth district about 4 km from town
items.note: Many houses let visitors try tie-dyeing the cloth themselves, kids can design their own pattern, and you take home a handkerchief or tote bag as a keepsake

items.activity: Do the dyeing and wait for the cloth to dry, then browse for mo hom shirts
items.note: Ask ahead which houses run workshops, since some take groups in set slots. The cost depends on the piece you make

items.activity: Lunch before heading off, and pick up khao kaep and crispy pork rinds as souvenirs
items.note: Khao kaep is a snack kids love, lightweight and easy to carry home
Leave some time for the kids to nap in the car so the trip ends without anyone worn out

items.name: Phae Mueang Phi
items.blurb: Earth pillars and cliffs in strange shapes, like a movie set. Kids love exploring it, the entry is cheap, and it doesn't take long.

items.name: The Pool Sky
items.blurb: A water park with a slide where kids can play all afternoon while parents sit at the cafe and watch up close.

items.name: The Phrae Farm
items.blurb: Open space, fruit gardens, and photo spots that let kids run around and burn off energy.

items.name: Mo hom dyeing workshop, Baan Thung Hong
items.blurb: Kids tie-dye the cloth themselves, design their own pattern, and take home a keepsake.

blocks.text: Easy foods for kids in Phrae

items.name: Khanom sen nam ngiao (clear broth / coconut broth)
items.blurb: Phrae's nam ngiao isn't heavily spiced. Order it with clear or coconut broth so kids can eat it, and keep the chili on the side.

items.name: Khao soi gai (chicken khao soi)
items.blurb: Noodles in a coconut curry broth, milder than other dishes. Order it without the roasted chili paste for kids.

items.name: Khao kaep
items.blurb: Thin, crispy rice crackers, a local snack. Kids love the crunch, and they make a good souvenir too.

items.name: Sai ua and pork rinds with sticky rice
items.blurb: Fragrant grilled herb sausage that's easy to eat with sticky rice, and kids can pick it up themselves.

items.name: Phrae-style noodle soup
items.blurb: A mild clear-broth noodle soup that's easy to order when kids don't feel like trying anything unfamiliar — a safe bet.

blocks.text: Tips for a smooth Phrae trip with kids

items: Start early, do the outdoor spots before noon — the sun is strong at Phae Mueang Phi and Cho Hae midday, so going early is more comfortable for kids and adults alike.
Plan no more than 3–4 stops a day — Phrae's sights are close together, true, but little kids tire fast, so leave time to rest and nap.
Pack the essentials — a hat, drinking water, wet wipes, and snacks in your bag for waits in line or when the kids get hungry on the road.
Your own car is the most flexible — Phae Mueang Phi, Cho Hae, and the farm are outside town, and public transport isn't convenient for families. Renting or chartering a car gives you more freedom.
Check the kids' cafe opening days first — some only open Saturday–Sunday, so call or check their page before you set out so you don't miss out.

faq.q: How many days are right for visiting Phrae with young kids?
faq.a: Three days and two nights is just about right, since the sights in and around town are close together and there's no long time in the car. Day one is the old town and teak mansions, day two covers Phae Mueang Phi and Cho Hae, and day three is the indigo-dyeing activity and souvenir shopping before you head home.

faq.q: Is Phae Mueang Phi suitable for kids? Is it dangerous?
faq.a: It's suitable for kids who can walk on their own; the path is sandy soil and easy to walk. Entry is 20 THB for adults and 10 THB for kids, open 08:00–17:00. That said, some viewpoints have fairly high edges, so keep a hand on small children and don't let them run near the edge.

faq.q: Can grandparents make it up to Wat Phra That Cho Hae? Is the walk manageable?
faq.a: It's easily manageable. Wat Phra That Cho Hae has a lift for the elderly and wheelchair users (20 THB), open 06:00–19:00, so you can take older relatives and small kids up to pay respects without climbing all the stairs.

faq.q: Is there anywhere in Phrae for kids to play in the water or run around?
faq.a: Yes. The Pool Sky is a cafe with a water-play area and a slide, around 99 THB per person with no time limit. The Phrae Farm is a farm cafe with open space where kids can run around. At both, parents can sit with a coffee and watch the kids up close.

faq.q: Can kids handle spicy northern food? Which dishes are easy for them?
faq.a: A lot of northern dishes are milder than you'd think. Khanom sen nam ngiao can be ordered with clear or coconut broth and the chili on the side; chicken khao soi and clear-broth noodle soup are also easy choices for kids. And the crispy khao kaep crackers are usually a hit and make a good souvenir.
